name: What design features help an open plan feel intentional?

mainEntity.name: How do you make an open floor plan feel designed instead of unfinished?
mainEntity.text: How do you make an open floor plan feel designed instead of unfinished?

acceptedAnswer.text: A successful open-floor-plan conversion should feel cohesive, not like a wall was simply removed. Design features such as layered lighting, repeated materials, aligned sight lines, built-ins, rugs, ceiling treatments, and coordinated cabinetry help define each area. The goal is to create flow while still giving the kitchen, dining, and living zones their own identity. Without these details, the room can feel oversized and undefined. Homeowners should ask for a plan that shows furniture placement, lighting layout, and how transitions will be handled at the opening. That makes the finished space feel purposeful and high-end rather than empty.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use consistent materials, a clear lighting plan, defined zones, trim details, and intentional furniture placement. Open spaces feel finished when each area still has a purpose and visual boundary.
